doc.title: Lou Donaldson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Coltrane followers and unemployment music
summary: He says avant-garde styles cannot get steady gigs in most American cities.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Well, actually, none of them played as well as they thought they was playing when they was high. I could have got somebody sober to play better. Because everybody was following Trane. But Trane jumped the track, and they jumped it right behind him. Now all of them are unemployed. I call that “unemployment music.” And they still play it. Disk jockeys and record companies are so stupid. They don’t even acknowledge it because they’re stupid.

Well, that’s a style of music that you can’t play in Atlanta. Charlotte, North Carolina. Birmingham. Big cities. St. Louis. You can’t play a steady gig there playing that. Kansas City. All the big cities. You can play it in New York, maybe one joint in Chicago— although Joe Segal has now started mixing up his entertainment. Nowhere in California can you play it, not on a steady gig. And that’s very counter-productive.
